description: Manifests a receiver MUST accept. `bytes` is the manifest, `fields` is what it decodes to, and `root` is the BLAKE3 hash of `bytes`. Encoding the fields gives `bytes` again. Sizes, times, offsets and lengths are decimal strings, because a JSON number does not hold a u64 in every language.

cases.name: the empty manifest
one file
one folder with nothing in it
a folder and a file in it
nested folders, each with an entry, and a file at the bottom
a file, a folder and a symlink together
a symlink that goes up with .. and stays inside the folder that was sent
a symlink with a deeper target, and one that goes down and back up
a file of no bytes
names in NFC with accents and non-Latin letters
byte order: a hyphen sorts before the slash that starts a child
byte order: upper case before lower case, and a two-byte letter after the ASCII ones
modes: none, the permission bits, and setuid, which a receiver does not apply
times and sizes at the edges of a u64, and varints of every length
one file packed into one pack
files in two packs, each filled to its last byte, with packed files of no bytes at the start and the end of the second
blob, packed, folder and symlink in one manifest
a small file left as a blob of its own next to a packed one, which rule 16 allows
a path of exactly 4096 bytes, with components of 255 bytes
hidden names, and names that only look like device names
names that are not the same under the comparison key: two letters, and ss against sss
the same letters in different folders are different paths
a symlink with a long target
